Oral Judgment:

1. This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "M.V. Act") by the Insurance Company against the Judgment and Award dated 29 th September, 2015, passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Amravati, (for short, "Tribunal) in Claim Petition No.410/2010 awarding the compensation of Rs.41,06,200/- against the Appellant-Insurance Company, the Owner and the Driver of the Taxi bearing No.MH-27/ C-5256.
2. The aforesaid Claim Petition was preferred by the Respondent nos.1 to 5 under Section 166 of the M.V. Act for compensation on account of death of Nisar Ahmed s/o Abdul Rahman in the motor vehicular accident on 24.07.2010 near Takharkheda-Shambhu fata on Amravati to Paratwada Road.
The Claim Petition was contested by the Appellant - Insurance Company by filing Written Statement.
The evidence was led by the Claimants.
No other party led the evidence.
By the impugned Judgment and Award, the learned Tribunal partly allowed the Claim Petition.
3. We have heard the learned Advocate for the Appellant, learned Advocate for the Claimants and learned Advocate for respondent no.6, the Vehicle Owner.

4. The learned Advocate for the Appellant submitted that, the Appeal is filed mainly on the ground that, Taxi Car was carrying more passengers than permitted or covered by the Insurance Policy and,
therefore, there was breach of Policy Conditions.
He submits that, the capacity of the Taxi was of five (5) passengers and the Occupants were in the said Taxi was more than five (5).
He submits that, due to Policy conditions by the Taxi owner and the Driver, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation and therefore, impugned Award be suitably modified.

5. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Claimants that, there were in all five (5) Claim Petitions before the learned Tribunal under Section 166 of the M.V Act by the Occupants of the said Taxi and the said Petitions were partly allowed.

The Insurance Company had preferred First Appeal before this Court bearing No. 688/2015 against the Judgment and Award in Claim Petition No.392/2010 which was filed by one of the Occupants of the said Taxi and the ground of breach of Policy was not raised in 4 fa725.2017 (j).odt
the said Appeal
. He submitted that, the said Appeal was dismissed by this Court by Judgment and Order dated 7th February, 2020.
He submits that, this Appeal be dismissed.

sentences.text: The learned Advocate for Respondent no.6 appearing online submits that, no fault can be found with the impugned Judgment and Award and the Appeal be dismissed.

7. There is no dispute that, the legal representatives of one of the Occupants of the said Taxi by name Mohd. Arif had preferred the Claim Petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act bearing no.392/2010,
which came to be partly allowed by the learned Tribunal on 11.7.2014.

It is not in dispute that, the Insurance Company which had preferred First Appeal No.688/2015 against the said decision of the Tribunal in the Claim Petition No.392/2010 and the said Appeal came to be dismissed.

There is nothing to show that, the Appellant Insurance Company had raised the ground of breach of Insurance Policy in the said Appeal, which was undisputedly connected Appeal arising out the same incident.
This being the undisputed factual aspect, the Ground no.(c) press in to service by learned Advocate for the Appellant in respect of breach of conditions does not survive.
Hence, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed.

Hence, the following order:-
5 fa725.2017 (j).odt ORDER (i) The Appeal stands dismissed with no order as to costs.
(ii) The amount of compensation deposited by the Insurance Company under the impugned Award is allowed to be withdrawn by the Claimants with interest accrued thereon, if not withdrawn earlier.
(iii) The Record and proceedings be sent back to the learned Tribunal.
(NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.) mukund ambulkar Signed by: Ambulkar (MLA) Designation: PS To Honourable Judge Date: 07/03/2026 12:03:24
